You had to have shown some pretty fine skills at the controls to lose him.|Ric Olié|[[Jar Jar 1|''Jar Jar'' 1]]}} '''Rum Sleg''' was a [[humanoid]] [[Gender|male]] [[bounty hunter]] who spent [[time]] in [[Mos Espa]] [[spaceport]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]] in [[32 BBY]]. While in the spaceport, he passed by a [[DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid]] shortly before attending the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing|podrace]] in the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena]]. He sat in the arena's stands and cheered for the [[Dug]] [[Podracer (profession)|podracer]] [[Sebulba]], who ultimately lost to the [[human]] racer [[Anakin Skywalker]]. During the [[Clone Wars]], Sleg and the bounty hunter [[Aurra Sing]] were hired to [[Death|kill]] the [[technician]] [[Mira Bridger]] after she created a [[fractal radio]] network. They [[Mission to Urubai|attacked]] her and her allies [[Kelleran Beq]], [[Jar Jar Binks]], and [[Coralisa Senig]] on the [[Planet|world]] [[Urubai]], but Senig shot Sleg in the shoulder and Bridger, Beq, and Binks escaped in the [[H-type Nubian yacht]] ''[[Heyblibber Duck]]''. With Sing having snuck on board the [[yacht]], Sleg gave chase in his own [[Rum Sleg's starship|ship]] and damaged the yacht while firing on it in [[orbit]]. However, the ''Heyblibber Duck'' managed to jump to [[lightspeed]] and escape from Sleg. ==Biography== ===Boonta Eve Classic=== [[File:RumSleg-Streets-TPM.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=Rum Sleg, in bright red armor, and a human in green and black armor talk in the streets of Mos Espa on Tatooine.|Rum Sleg (bottom right) was in Mos Espa during the Boonta Eve Classic.]] Rum Sleg was a [[humanoid]] [[Gender|male]] who worked as a [[bounty hunter]] during the reign of the [[Galactic Republic]].{{Film|I}} In [[32 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|I}} to [[32 BBY]]. Sleg stood and spoke to a [[human]] in the streets of the [[Mos Espa]] [[spaceport]]{{Databank|mos-espa|Mos Espa}} on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. He then began walking through the streets and passed a [[DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid|DK-1 Dark Eye probe droid]]''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' that had been sent out by the [[Sith apprentice]] [[Maul|Darth Maul]] to search for [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] of the planet [[Naboo]]. The [[bounty]] hunter later attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[podracing]] event and sat in the stands at the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena]], where each of the three laps of the race started and ended. Sleg cheered when the [[Dug]] [[Podracer (profession)|podracer]] [[Sebulba]] passed through the arena in the lead after the first lap of the race; however, during the final lap, the Dug crashed and was beaten by the [[human]] podracer [[Anakin Skywalker]]. ===The Urubai job=== {{Quote|I picked up some chatter on the network. Apparently, the mere ''existence'' of a fractal radio network has the chancellor… ''displeased''.''"
"''Yousa haven't broken any laws. Mesa don't tink…''"
"''You're right. I haven't done anything ''illegal''. But my work ''threatens'' a lot of powerful people. And I've heard that ''someone'' has hired two ''bounty hunters'' to ''kill'' me.|Mira Bridger and Jar Jar Binks|}} [[File:SlegAndSing-JarJar1.png|thumb|left|300px|alt=Rum Sleg and Aurra Sing firing with their blasters in a rocky canyon on Urubai.|Rum Sleg and Aurra Sing were hired to kill Mira Bridger.]] During the [[Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Sleg and his fellow bounty hunter [[Aurra Sing]]—who had also attended the Boonta Eve Classic the same [[Standard year|year]] as Sleg—were hired to [[Death|kill]] [[Mira Bridger]], a member of the [[Unseen]] faction on the [[planet]] [[Urubai]] who had created a [[fractal radio]] network. Although not illegal, the existence of the private and secure communications network threatened a lot of powerful individuals and displeased [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] of the Republic. Despite learning of Sleg and Aurra's assignment to kill her, Bridger refused to leave her work and remained on Urubai until [[Jedi Master]] [[Kelleran Beq]] and [[Junior Representative]] [[Jar Jar Binks]] of the [[Galactic Senate|Republic's Senate]] [[Mission to Urubai|convinced]] her to leave with them. Sleg and Sing located Bridger as she, Beq, Binks, and her [[Urubaian]] ally [[Coralisa Senig]] approached Binks' [[H-type Nubian yacht]], the ''[[Heyblibber Duck]]''. The two bounty hunters opened fire on their target and her allies, but Beq was able to deflect their shots with his [[Kelleran Beq's lightsaber|lightsaber]], providing cover for the others as they ran toward the [[starship]]. Despite Beq's efforts, Senig took a shot to the [[Limb|knee]] and was downed but began returning fire from the ground with her [[blaster pistol]] to cover her allies' escape, urging them to leave her behind. One of her shots caught Sleg in the left shoulder, causing him to grunt in pain. Beq, Binks, and Bridger then safely made it to the ''Heyblibber Duck'' and boarded, but Sing was able to leap aboard as well before they took off. [[File:SlegShot-JarJar1.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=In the left panel, Coralisa Senig aims and shoots her blaster pistol while lying on her front on the dirt of Urubai. In the second panel, Rum Sleg grunts as Senig's shot hits him in the shoulder while he and Aurra Sing behind him continue firing.|Coralisa Senig shot Rum Sleg in the shoulder on Urubai.]] Sleg then boarded his own [[Rum Sleg's starship|ship]] and gave chase into [[orbit]], opening fire on the ''Heyblibber Duck''. Sleg caused enough damage to wound the [[yacht]]'s [[pilot]], [[Ric Olié]], in the [[cockpit]], forcing Binks to take over flying while Beq fought Sing. Sleg continued firing on the yacht as the inexperienced Binks struggled to control it, but the bounty hunter's target escaped when Binks managed to jump to [[lightspeed]] on Beq's orders. The ''Heyblibber Duck'' then got Bridger safely to [[Coruscant]], [[capital]] of the Republic. Once there, a recovered Olié assumed that it had been Beq who outflew Sleg, but the [[Jedi]] assured him it was Binks. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Ghng—!|Rum Sleg is shot in the shoulder.|}} Rum Sleg was reputed to be a skilled pilot and was known to Ric Olié, although he was evaded by the inexperienced Binks after being shot in the shoulder. ==Equipment== [[File:RumSlegShipBattle-JarJar1.png|thumb|left|300px|alt=Rum Sleg's gray and red starship fires on the rear of the silver ''Heyblibber Duck'' in space.|Rum Sleg's starship was marked with a skull.]] Rum Sleg wore a painted-[[Bone|skull]] visor to cover his face, along with a [[Color|red]]-and-black suit of [[armor]], including a [[helmet]] and a silver [[backpack]]. He also carried a silver blaster pistol [[holster]]ed on his [[belt]]. While fighting on Urubai, he used a pair of black blaster pistols, with the right weapon wrapped to his wrist with white cloth. The bounty hunter flew a gray starship with red patterning and a large white skull on the front. ==Behind the scenes== ===Filming=== {{Quote|In 1998, I was working at ILM's "Rebel Mac Unit". One day, someone came in and said "Come with me"… we walked over to Windward Stage where I was given essentially a scuba suit with helmet and accessories.|Alex Lindsay|{{Twitter|alexlindsay|1389579359577526273|[[Alex Lindsay]]|quote=In 1998, I was working at ILM's "Rebel Mac Unit". One day, someone came in and said "Come with me"... we walked over to Windward Stage where I was given essentially a scuba suit with helmet and accessories. Here's how it ended up... May the Fourth be with you.|archivedate=20210505073505}}}} [[File:Rum_Sleg_at_the_races.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=Rum Sleg and a humanoid in yellow and black armor sit together in the stands of the Mos Espa Grand Arena cheering.|Rum Sleg was portrayed by different actors in his two separate scenes.]] Rum Sleg first appeared as a background character in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. For the scene in the streets of Mos Espa, he was portrayed by [[Industrial Light & Magic]] digital effects artist [[Alex Lindsay]], who in [[1998]] was brought to the Windward Stage and given what he describes as a "scuba suit with helmet and accessories." He was then filmed in the costume walking and talking with{{YouTube|video=0ZFelHqtlFU|text=MBW's Alex Lindsay Was in Star Wars|channel=channel/UCwY9B5_8QDGP8niZhBtTh8w|name=TWiT Tech Podcast Network}} fellow digital effects artist [[Jonathan Rothbart]], although Rothbart was then rotoscoped out of the shot so that Sleg seemed to be walking alone. Lindsay says this was possibly because you could see too much of Rothbart's face. After filming the scene, Lindsay was asked to "t-pose" for photographs that could then be used to make an action figure, and ultimately one was released in [[2009]] as part of the ''[[Star Wars: The Legacy Collection]]'' toyline.{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Legacy Collection|pack=#09: Rum Sleg|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLCBD09RumSleg.asp}} He believes he was picked to portray the character simply because he was the right size for the suit, but did not get to keep the costume after filming and doubts it would have held up well. A separate actor portrayed Sleg viewing the podrace. ===Naming and the Light Side=== {{Quote|I was running the RPG on my kitchen table in Virginia Beach, and everybody named their own characters, of course. Dan's was named "Rum Sleg," and his battle cry was "Just Chill"!|Chuck Kallenbach|{{Twitter|chuckkallenbach|status/1315052864205537280|[[Chuck Kallenbach]]|quote=Absolutely. I was running the RPG on my kitchen table in Virginia Beach, and everybody named their own characters, of course. Dan's was named "Rum Sleg," and his battle cry was "Just Chill"! Is that all you need? {{C|In response to "Hi Chuck, could you confirm on here that Rum Sleg was named after Dan Bojanowski's Star Wars RPG character? We need something outside Wookieepedia to reference it to!"}}|archiveurl=https://archive.is/RGfJ9}}}} For the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Rum Sleg's name was used in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile card game]] ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'', which initially launched in [[2013]]. Although the launch of ''Force Collection'' predates{{SW|url=news/announcing-star-wars-force-collection|text=Announcing Star Wars: Force Collection|nolive=1}} the ''Star Wars'' canon reset of [[2014]],{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}} [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Leland Chee]] confirmed that the game was kept updated to fit with canon.{{Twitter|holocronkeeper|status/846807700482666496|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=I'm not gonna go through the trouble of changing them and I don't have any reason to believe currently that anyone would. […] On the off-chance that we DID have a current need to change any of these, we would have for Force Collection.|archivedate=20210505080831}} — [[Leland Chee]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] has confirmed that [[in-universe]] information from ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' conforms with ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]]. [[File:LightSide-Insider201.png|thumb|left|300px|alt=A protocol droid introduces Boba Fett to a class of baby versions of various Star Wars characters including Malakili, Jaxxon T. Tumperakki, Jar Jar Binks, Greedo, Ponda Baba, Cornelius Evazan, Jabba Desilijic Tiure, Babu Frik, Chewbacca, Orrimaarko, and Rum Sleg|A baby version of Rum Sleg appeared in "The Light Side."]] The character's name originated in the [[Boonta Eve Podrace (YJCCG)|''Boonta Eve Podrace'']] expansion set of the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Young Jedi Collectible Card Game]], released by [[Decipher]] in [[2001]].{{YJCCG|set=Boonta Eve Podrace|cardname=Rum Sleg|link=boontaevepodrace/dark/large/44rumslegbountyhunter.html}} According to Decipher employee{{JKTCG|set=Premiere|parent=1|bypass=1}} [[Chuck Kallenbach]], Sleg was named after a character that fellow Decipher employee [[Dan Bojanowski]] played in a ''Star Wars'' roleplaying game that Kallenbach ran. The character's catch phrase was "Just Chill!" A baby version of Sleg holding an [[ice cream]] cone was included as part of a class of various "baby" versions of ''Star Wars'' characters in [[Jamie Cosley]]'s "[[Launchpad|The Light Side]]" comic in the [[Star Wars Insider 201|two hundred-and-first]] issue of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine, which was published by [[Titan Magazines]]{{InsiderCite|201|Launchpad}} on [[March 30]], [[2021]].{{TitanComics|url=m/68-star-wars-insider-201|text=Star Wars Insider #201}} In the comic panel, the class is being introduced by a [[protocol droid]] to [[Boba Fett]], who refuses to take on the group but claims to know [[Din Djarin|someone else]] who will. ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Rum Sleg}} *{{Film|I}} {{1st}} *[[Jar Jar 1|''Jar Jar'' 1]] ==Sources== *{{ForceCollection|Rum Sleg|star=2}} {{1stID|Rum Sleg}} *{{InsiderCite|201|Launchpad}} {{Po}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |es=Rum Sleg |fr=Rum Sleg |ja=ラム・スレッグ }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sleg, Rum}} [[Category:Bounty hunters]] [[Category:Humanoids]] [[Category:Individuals with he/him pronouns]] [[Category:Males]]
